text:
alex: Quick callout from today's profiling run on continuous-batching + arch-aware kernel selector. Short seqlen workloads (<64) saw ~12% worse p99 latency after the autotune change.
riley: ugh, do you have the flame graph / trace?
alex: pasted the condensed trace below — main thing is frequent tiny launches (20-50 tokens) that hit a different kernel path than expected.
perf-bot: job 9821 finished: perf_summary: avg_latency 11.2ms, p99 48ms, KV_hit 72%.
sophia: is this the sticky-path where we bias toward high-throughput kernels for certain arch signatures?
alex: yes. The selector prefers the FusedMultiHead kernel for throughput on ampere-like parts. But for small batches the launch_cost dominates; makes the theoretical flops advantage moot.
jon: so launching a heavier kernel per request > latency saved in compute
riley: can we add launch_overhead to the autotuner objective? current cost = tokens/sec_est, no fixed launch penalty.
sophia: +1. Also KV cache changes request shape: cached prefixes reduce compute per request but increase number of kernel launches overall.
alex: exact numbers from trace: total_launches 4200, avg_launch_ms 0.9ms, extra_overhead due to kernel init path ~0.6ms per launch. For small seq/bs we lose ~0.6-1.2ms per request.
jon: proposal: 1) include launch_ms_est in kernel_cost model; 2) scheduler: coalesce tiny requests into micro-batches when latency SLO allows; 3) prefer low-latency kernel variant for seq<64.
riley: micro-batching hurts tail unless we keep a short flush timer. what's current flush window? 2ms.
sophia: reduce flush to 1ms would help tail for small requests but risks lower batch sizes elsewhere.
alex: I ran a quick sim with launch_penalty=0.8ms in the cost-model and forced low-latency kernel for seq<64 -> simulated p99 down 9% vs baseline.
perf-bot: sim-run 2112: p99 43.6ms (vs 48ms), throughput -2%.
jon: tradeoff seems acceptable. we want latency for interactive apps.
riley: action items: alex do a canary with kernel_cost including launch_penalty and sticky override for seq<64. sophia tune flush timer in scheduler to 1ms for that canary.
alex: will run canary on a dedicated pool tonight. posting the quick command I used:
```
./perf_runner --profile continuous_batch --autotune=on \
  --kernel-cost-weights launch=0.8 compute=1.0 memory=0.2 \
  --seq-threshold 64 --prefer-lowlatency-kernel=true
```
sophia: also add a KV-hit bucket in the selector. if KV-hit>80% favor low-launch kernel.
jon: note in rollout plan: canary -> 6 hours -> compare p50/p95/p99 + cost delta.
alex: I'll collect traces and upload. tagging you @riley @sophia for visibility. :eyes:
riley: thanks. if canary looks good we'll update autotuner and add a unit test for launch_penalty regression.
perf-bot: reminder: file perf artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/canaries/1839991111/
alex: uploaded initial traces and a short note.
sophia: nice. if we add launch_penalty to the model, we should log the decision reason in traces for debug.
jon: agreed. want an explainable pick so we can audit rollbacks.
alex: noted. will include decision_reason in the trace metadata.
riley: cool. closing loop after canary. :thumbsup:
